subject: The presence of malignant cells in the pleural fluid and/or pleural tissue
object: the presence of disseminated or advanced cancer and is associated with a lower life expectancy.

subject: In malignant pleural effusion, survival
object: 5.5 months for lung cancer patients in a recent study, whereas overall survival for all types of cancer ranged from 3 to 12 months, depending on the type of tumour and the patient's comorbidities.

subject: Malignant pleural effusion
object: 15% of oncology patients; as many as 50,000 new cases are diagnosed every year in the UK and 150,000 in the USA, with hospitalisation costs of more than five billion dollars.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020

subject: Most malignant pleural effusions
object: symptomatic and frequently cause dyspnoea, which is associated not only with the size of the effusion but also with how fast the fluid accumulates and with underlying cardio-respiratory comorbidities.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Most MPE are symptomatic and frequently cause dyspnea, which is not only associated with the size of the PE, but also associated with the rate of fluid accumulation and the presence of underlying cardio-respiratory comorbidities.

subject: Other symptoms of malignant pleural effusion
object: chest pain, dry cough, or early satiety due to the pressure the effusion puts on the stomach.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Other symptoms include chest pain, dry cough, or early feeling of satiety due to the pressure exerted by the PE on the stomach .

subject: A suspected pleural effusion
object: at a volume of 200 mL, and a lateral chest X-ray can detect as little as 50 mL of pleural fluid, seen as a costophrenic angle effusion.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: A suspicion of PE can be radiographically confirmed at a volume of 200 mL. In addition, chest X-ray can detect as little as 50 mL of PF on a lateral view, which will show a costophrenic angle effusion .

subject: A massive, loculated pleural effusion with reduced volume of the lung on the same side
object: also suggestive of malignant pleural effusion.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: A massive, loculated PE and a reduced volume of the ipsilateral lung are also suggestive of MPE.

subject: In a retrospective study of more than 62,000 thoracenteses for pleural effusion of any cause, chest ultrasound
object: the risk of pneumothorax by 19% (OR 0.81; 95% CI 0.74 to 0.90), so thoracic ultrasound, which has no associated complications, is recommended before thoracentesis.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: A retrospective study of more than 62,000 thoracocenteses for all-cause PE showed that chest ultrasound reduced the risk for pneumothorax by 19% (OR = 0.81; 95% CI = 0.74–0.90) . Therefore, it is recommended that thoracic ultrasound, which has no associated complications, is performed prior to thoracentesis.

subject: Thoracic ultrasound
object: a malignant pleural effusion when it finds pleural thickening over 1 cm, diaphragmatic nodules or diaphragmatic thickening over 7 mm, visceral pleural thickening, or pleural irregularity or nodularity.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Thoracic ultrasound can also suggest an MPE based on the finding of pleural thickening (>1 cm), diaphragmatic nodules or diaphragmatic thickening >7 mm, visceral pleura thickening, or pleural irregularity/nodularity .

subject: CT
object: high specificity but low sensitivity for separating benign from malignant pleural effusion, and mesothelioma from pleural metastasis; in one study its positive and negative predictive values for malignant effusion were 80% (95% CI 75 to 86%) and 65% (95% CI 58 to 72%), meaning one in three patients suspected of having a malignant effusion will have it despite a negative CT scan.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Computerized tomography (CT) has high specificity but low sensitivity to separate benign PE from MPE, and mesothelioma from pleural metastasis . The positive and negative predictive value of CT to identify MPE were 80% (CI 95%: 75–86%) and 65%, respectively (CI 95%: 58–72%). This means that one in three patients suspected to have an MPE will have it despite a negative CT scan .

subject: Cytology
object: the initial test in diagnosing malignant pleural effusion; its diagnostic performance is close to 60%, with very low sensitivity for mesothelioma (6%) and high sensitivity for adenocarcinomas (79%).
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Cytology is the initial test in establishing a diagnosis of MPE. The diagnostic performance of cytology is close to 60% , with very low sensitivity for mesothelioma (6%) and high for adenocarcinomas (79%) .

subject: The low diagnostic performance of pleural fluid cytology
object: the tumour not always being on the surface of the mesothelial cells, where malignant cells are shed into the pleural fluid; it may also involve the layer below the serous layer, so only a few malignant cells reach the pleural space.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: 2.2. Cytology of Pleural Fluid The low diagnostic performance of this procedure is due to the fact that the tumour is not always located in the surface of mesothelial cells, where malignant cells will be exfoliated in PF, but they may also involve the layer below the serous layer; therefore, only a few malignant cells will reach the pleural space.

subject: Immunohistochemistry
object: reactive mesothelial cells from the cells of malignant pleural mesothelioma and of adenocarcinoma metastases, by exposing them to different antibody panels, as each has specific antigens.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Immunohistochemistry can help differentiate reactive mesothelial cells from those of malignant pleural mesothelioma and adenocarcinoma metastases, exposing them to different antibody panels, as each of them has specific antigens.

subject: Pleural biopsy
object: the gold standard procedure for diagnosing malignant pleural effusion; percutaneous pleural biopsy has a lower diagnostic sensitivity (46%) than cytology because malignant infiltrates of the parietal pleura are patchy, but its sensitivity can reach 87 to 94% under ultrasound or CT guidance.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Pleural biopsy is the gold standard procedure for the diagnosis of MPE . Percutaneous pleural biopsy has a lower diagnostic sensitivity than cytology, as malignant parietal pleura infiltrates have a patchy pattern (46%) . Its sensitivity, however, can reach 87–94% under ultrasound or CT guidance .

subject: Medical thoracoscopy
object: a safe procedure with low complication and mortality rates and high diagnostic performance; medical and surgical thoracoscopy perform similarly, with low mortality (0 to 0.34%) and major complication rates (1.2 to 1.8%).
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Medical thoracoscopy is a safe procedure with low rates of complications and mortality and with a high diagnostic performance. The performance of these procedures (medical or surgical thoracoscopy) is similar and mortality and major complication rates are low (between 0–0.34% and 1.2–1.8%, respectively ).

subject: A trapped lung (one that does not re-expand to its normal position, with raised pleural elastance)
object: the failure of pleurodesis, because the two layers of the pleura cannot come together enough.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Its relevance is that the trapped lung (the lung does not reexpand to its normal position and the pleural elastance is elevated) is related to the failure of pleurodesis, since there is not a sufficient apposition between the pleural leaves.

subject: Predicting survival in a patient with malignant pleural effusion
object: a better choice of treatment; tools such as the LENT score, based on pleural fluid lactate dehydrogenase, the ECOG performance score, the neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio and the type of tumour, have been developed and validated to estimate the risk of mortality from the score obtained.
source: Article: Ferreiro L, Suárez-Antelo J, Álvarez-Dobaño JM et al. Malignant Pleural Effusion: Diagnosis and Management. Canadian Respiratory Journal 2020
source_quote: Predicting the survival expectancy of a patient with MPE can contribute to a better therapeutic choice. Some tools have been developed and validated to assess the risk of mortality, such as the LENT score, based on lactate dehydrogenase in PF, the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance score, the neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio, and type of tumour (Table 1), which estimates the risk of mortality based on the score obtained .

subject: In the LENT prognostic score for malignant pleural effusions, the risk categories
object: low risk (total score 0 to 1, median survival 319 days), moderate risk (score 2 to 4, median survival 130 days) and high risk (score 5 to 7, median survival 44 days).

subject: Local anaesthetic thoracoscopy (LAT)
object: mainly to find out whether a malignant process is present in the pleural space; case series suggest it has a 92.6% diagnostic sensitivity in malignant pleural disease.
source: Article: Li D, Jackson K, Panchal R et al. Local Anaesthetic Thoracoscopy for Pleural Effusion—A Narrative Review. Healthcare 2022
source_quote: LAT is performed predominantly to determine if a malignant process is present in the pleural space. Various case series would suggest that it has a 92.6% diagnostic sensitivity in malignant pleural disease .

subject: A positive pleural fluid cytology
object: in certain cancers, breast and ovarian cancers being most likely to give one, than in others such as malignant pleural mesothelioma, where pleural fluid cytology typically has a low diagnostic yield of 6 to 32% and parietal pleura is often needed to characterise the tumour fully.
source: Article: Li D, Jackson K, Panchal R et al. Local Anaesthetic Thoracoscopy for Pleural Effusion—A Narrative Review. Healthcare 2022
source_quote: However, a positive cytological result is more likely in certain type of cancers (with breast and ovarian cancers being most likely to provide positive pleural fluid cytology) than others such as malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) . In MPM, pleural fluid cytology typically has a low diagnostic yield of 6–32%, and parietal pleura is often required for full characterisation of the tumour .

subject: Pleural infection
object: stages: first a simple exudate, then a fibrinopurulent stage, then an organising stage with pleural peel formation; local anaesthetic thoracoscopy is only feasible at stages 1 and 2, with division of adhesions, drainage of fluid and placement of a chest tube.
source: Article: Li D, Jackson K, Panchal R et al. Local Anaesthetic Thoracoscopy for Pleural Effusion—A Narrative Review. Healthcare 2022
source_quote: LAT is only feasible in pleural infection at stage 1 and 2, which are the first two stages of pleural infection (simple exudate then fibrinopurulent stage and then an organising stage with pleural peel formation) with division of adhesions, drainage of fluid and placement of a chest tube .

subject: Before local anaesthetic thoracoscopy, careful patient selection
object: a detailed history of the disease process, including previous occupational exposure (such as asbestos) and previous malignant disease, is important.
source: Article: Li D, Jackson K, Panchal R et al. Local Anaesthetic Thoracoscopy for Pleural Effusion—A Narrative Review. Healthcare 2022
source_quote: Careful patient selection is required prior to LAT: a detailed history regarding the disease process including previous occupational exposure (e.g., asbestos) and previous malignant disease is important.

subject: In tuberculous pleural disease, local anaesthetic thoracoscopy
object: up to 100% diagnostic sensitivity but is very resource intensive, which precludes its use in many countries; in areas where tuberculosis is highly prevalent, a combination of pleural fluid adenosine deaminase, differential cell count and closed pleural biopsy is just as effective.
source: Article: Li D, Jackson K, Panchal R et al. Local Anaesthetic Thoracoscopy for Pleural Effusion—A Narrative Review. Healthcare 2022
source_quote: As an aside, in tuberculous pleural disease, LAT has up to 100% diagnostic sensitivity, but LAT is very resource intensive, and that precludes its use in many countries . A combination of pleural fluid adenosine deaminase, differential cell count and closed pleural biopsy is just as effective in areas of high prevalence of tuberculosis .

subject: Tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE)
object: currently the most common form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, and is more often seen in endemic areas, especially in people co-infected with HIV, consistent with the higher risk of tuberculosis in immunocompromised patients.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: Tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) is currently the most common form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis (TB) . It is more frequently observed in endemic areas, especially in individuals co-infected with HIV, consistent with epidemiological data indicating a higher risk of TB in immunocompromised patients .

subject: Tuberculous pleural effusion
object: a primary infection acquired in the preceding 6 to 12 weeks or, more commonly, from reactivation of latent tuberculosis triggered by diseases (such as solid or haematological malignancies) or systemic treatments (prolonged steroids, antiblastic and biologic therapies) that depress cell-mediated immunity.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: TPE may result from a primary infection acquired within the preceding 6–12 weeks or, more commonly, from reactivation of latent TB, triggered by diseases (ie. solid haematologic malignancies) or systemic treatments (prolonged steroids, antiblastic and biologic therapies) associated with depressed cell-mediated immune response .

subject: In industrialised countries, tuberculous pleural effusion
object: a post-primary manifestation, occurring at a later mean age than reported in other regions.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: In industrialized countries, however, it typically represents a post-primary manifestation, occurring at a later mean age compared to that reported in other regions .

subject: In tuberculous pleural effusion, the underlying mechanism
object: a T-cell-mediated hypersensitivity reaction after mycobacterial antigens enter the pleural space, often after subpleural caseating granulomas rupture; the antigens trigger inflammation that increases capillary permeability and osmotic transudation of proteins and fluid into the pleural cavity, and the inflammation, first dominated by neutrophils and then by T lymphocytes, obstructs pleural lymphatic channels and slows fluid reabsorption.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: The underlying pathogenic mechanism involves a T-cell–mediated hypersensitivity reaction following the entry of mycobacterial antigens into the pleural space, often after the rupture of subpleural caseating granulomas. The presence of these antigens triggers an inflammatory response, leading to increased capillary permeability and osmotic transudation of proteins and fluid into the pleural cavity. The ensuing inflammation, initially dominated by neutrophils and subsequently by T lymphocytes, impairs lymphatic drainage by obstructing pleural lymphatic channels, thereby slowing fluid reabsorption.

subject: In tuberculous pleural effusion, strong infiltration of Th1-type T cells
object: a localised immune microenvironment (compartmentalisation), which explains both the low bacterial load and the low yield of mycobacterial cultures from pleural fluid.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: The robust infiltration of Th1-type T cells creates a localized immune microenvironment, referred to as compartmentalization, which explains both the paucibacillary nature of TPE and the low yield of mycobacterial cultures obtained from pleural fluid .

subject: Tuberculous pleural effusions
object: appear pale yellow and are exudates, and cytology characteristically shows lymphocytosis, with lymphocytes making up more than 50% of total nucleated cells and in most cases more than 75%.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: TPE typically appear pale yellow and are classified as exudates. Cytological analysis characteristically reveals lymphocytosis, with lymphocytes accounting for more than 50% of the total nucleated cells, and in most cases, exceeding 75%.

subject: Tuberculous pleural effusion
object: a high neutrophil count in the very early stages of disease or in later stages consistent with empyema; lymphocytes become predominant after the initial immune response, usually about two weeks after the hypersensitivity reaction begins.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: It is worth noting, however, that TPE is typically characterized by a high neutrophil count during the very early stages of disease or in later stages consistent with empyema . Lymphocytes become predominant in the phases following the initial immune response, usually after approximately two weeks from the onset of the hypersensitivity reaction .

subject: Uncomplicated tuberculous pleural fluid
object: a pH above 7.3 and, consistent with an exudate, raised lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) compared with serum and a protein concentration that may exceed 5 g/dL.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: When uncomplicated, the pleural fluid usually has a pH above 7.3. Consistent with the features of exudates, TPE fluid shows elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels compared to serum and a protein concentration that may exceed 5 g/dL.

subject: Adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme made and released by activated T lymphocytes,
object: a low-cost, widely available and clinically valuable biomarker, and pleural fluid ADA is considered highly sensitive and specific for tuberculous pleural effusion, particularly above a diagnostic threshold of 40 U/L.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: In this context, adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme produced and released by activated T lymphocytes, represents a low-cost, widely accessible, and clinically valuable biomarker. ADA measurement in pleural fluid is considered both highly sensitive and specific for TPE, particularly when levels exceed a diagnostic threshold of 40 U/L .

subject: A lymphocyte-predominant exudate with raised adenosine deaminase (ADA)
object: highly suggestive of tuberculosis in high-prevalence settings; in low-prevalence regions, the absence of lymphocyte predominance and raised ADA makes tuberculosis unlikely, and pleural biopsy should be considered to confirm the diagnosis.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: A lymphocyte-predominant exudate combined with elevated ADA levels is highly suggestive of tuberculosis in high-prevalence settings. On the contrary, in low-prevalence regions, the absence of lymphocyte predominance and elevated ADA levels makes a tuberculous etiology unlikely, and pleural biopsy should be considered to confirm the diagnosis.

subject: Raised adenosine deaminase (ADA)
object: non-tuberculous empyemas, which can give false positives; then a pleural fluid lymphocyte-to-neutrophil ratio above 0.75 is more strongly suggestive of tuberculous pleural effusion and can greatly improve specificity.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: Nonetheless, elevated ADA levels may also be observed in non-tuberculous empyemas, potentially leading to false-positive interpretations . In such cases, diagnostic specificity can be significantly enhanced by assessing the pleural fluid lymphocyte-to-neutrophil ratio, with values greater than 0.75 being more strongly suggestive of TPE .

subject: Tuberculous pleural effusion
object: acutely, particularly in younger immunocompetent people, or follow a more subacute course; the most common clinical features are pleuritic chest pain, non-productive cough, fever, night sweats, dyspnoea and weight loss, and the effusion is typically unilateral and can vary widely in size.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: TPE may present acutely, particularly in younger, immunocompetent individuals, or follow a more subacute course . The most common clinical manifestations include pleuritic chest pain, nonproductive cough, fever, night sweats, dyspnoea, and weight loss . The effusion is typically unilateral and can vary widely in size.

subject: Patients with tuberculous pleural effusion
object: younger than those with pulmonary tuberculosis, although in industrialised countries tuberculous pleuritis more often reflects reactivation and patients tend to be older; even when symptoms are mild, up to 65% of these cases may progress to active pulmonary tuberculosis within two years, which makes early diagnosis and prompt treatment important.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: Patients with TPE are generally younger than those with pulmonary tuberculosis; however, in industrialized countries, tuberculous pleuritis more commonly reflects reactivation disease, and the average patient age tends to be higher . Although some individuals experience only mild symptoms, up to 65% of these cases may progress to active pulmonary tuberculosis within two years, underscoring the importance of early diagnosis and prompt initiation of therapy .

subject: Because tuberculous pleural effusion develops from a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to mycobacterial antigens, the bacterial load in the pleural space
object: typically low, which explains why direct microscopy and culture of the fluid are often negative (diagnostic yield 5 to 10% for pleural fluid AFB smear and 30 to 50% for culture).

Therefore, the bacterial load in the pleural space is typically low, which explains why direct microscopy and culture of the fluid are often negative (the diagnostic yield is 5–10% for pleural fluid AFB smear and 30–50% for culture) .

subject: Because tuberculous pleural effusion comes from a delayed hypersensitivity reaction and the bacterial load in the pleural space is typically low, so that fluid microscopy and culture are often negative (yield 5 to 10% for AFB smear and 30 to 50% for culture), pleural biopsy
object: the most reliable tool for a definitive diagnosis, which rests on finding Mycobacterium tuberculosis in pleural fluid or biopsy specimens, or on histological evidence of epithelioid cell granulomas and/or caseating granulomas.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025

Therefore, the bacterial load in the pleural space is typically low, which explains why direct microscopy and culture of the fluid are often negative (the diagnostic yield is 5–10% for pleural fluid AFB smear and 30–50% for culture) . This makes pleural biopsy the most reliable tool for achieving a definitive diagnosis , which is based on the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in pleural fluid or biopsy specimens, or on histopathological evidence of epithelioid cell granulomas and/or caseating granulomas.

subject: On medical thoracoscopy for suspected tuberculous pleural effusion, the most common abnormalities
object: diffuse pale micronodules on a hyperaemic background, giving a "strawberry-like" pleural surface, and "sago-like" nodules resembling sago pearls, a pattern considered highly specific for tuberculous involvement.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: During MT performed in cases of suspected TPE, several distinct endoscopic patterns can be observed. The most common abnormalities include diffuse pale micronodules on a hyperemic background, which give the pleural surface a “strawberry-like” appearance (Fig. 6), and “sago-like” nodules, so called due to its resemblance to sago pearls (Fig. 7). This pattern is considered highly specific for tuberculous involvement .

subject: The high rate of immigration into countries with low tuberculosis prevalence
object: more frequent atypical endoscopic patterns of tuberculous pleurisy, which differ from the classic "strawberry-like" pleura and may closely mimic malignant pleural involvement, making the differential diagnosis difficult.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: The high rate of immigration in countries with low tuberculosis prevalence has led to an increasingly frequent observation of atypical endoscopic patterns of tuberculous pleurisy. These presentations differ from the classic “strawberry-like” pleura and may closely mimic malignant pleural involvement, thus posing significant challenges in the differential diagnosis.

subject: Medical thoracoscopy, which gives the highest diagnostic yield for both pleural malignancy and tuberculosis and is considered the gold standard,
object: easily accessible in low-resource settings, where repeating an ultrasound-guided thoracentesis may be a reasonable alternative before proceeding to pleural biopsy.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
source_quote: Although MT offers the highest diagnostic yield for both pleural malignancy and TB and is considered the gold standard, it may not be easily accessible in low-resource settings. In these contexts, repeating an ultrasound-guided thoracentesis may be a reasonable alternative before proceeding to pleural biopsy.

subject: Tuberculosis
object: a significant challenge for modern medicine and is the world's leading cause of death from a single infectious agent.
source: Article: Inchingolo R, Carriera L, Ielo S et al. Tuberculous pleural effusion: integrating thoracic ultrasound and medical thoracoscopy in the diagnosis and management: a pictorial narrative review and an algorithm proposal. Journal of Ultrasound 2025
